critical_code_review_comments: recruitment_service.dispose: for outcome=connected_interested when target stays in ACTIVE_STATUSES and no next_followup and no existing next_followup, the code correctly forces 'This lead is still active — schedule the next follow-up'. But if the lead ALREADY has a pending future next_followup_at, that pending followup will be silently marked 'done' (elif connected branch) once the disposition saves — user has no explicit UI hint that the existing follow-up will be closed. Consider surfacing this in the modal.

recruitment_service.dispose validation flow: connected_interested moves an already-past-'contacted' lead nowhere (target=cur). If cur='not_interested' it stays not_interested silently — user might expect a bounce-back to interested. Consider warning when outcome semantics conflict with current status.

recruitment_service.auto_distribute: pool includes 'team_leader' role (line 552). Round-robin across recruiters + team-leaders may hand leads to TL — verify this matches business intent (spec says 'active recruiters in scope'). If not, restrict to role='recruiter'.

recruitment_service.assign_leads: does NOT enforce that target owner has leads.view_own permission or is a recruiter — could technically assign a lead to any active user (e.g. an accountant if one existed with is_active=true). Consider filtering by role in ['recruiter','team_leader'].
recruitment_routes.list_leads: uses require_permission only implicitly via internal check; other endpoints in this router use require_permission decorator. Consistent style is better.
recruitment_routes.export_leads: audit record captured after CSV generation — if generation succeeds but response send fails, the audit already claims 'exported'. Minor.

models.recruitment.DispositionCreate: status_override accepts ANY LEAD_STATUS, bypassing ALLOWED_TRANSITIONS guard (dispose() doesn't re-check ALLOWED_TRANSITIONS when status_override is present). An admin could override 'joined' back to 'new' via a call disposition. Consider running the same transition validation.

recruitment_service.dispose: target='selected' requires expected_joining_date (good) but does not require closure/joining record to satisfy REASON_REQUIRED — fine. However there is no explicit block on outcome=connected_interested paired with a status_override to 'joined' without an interview or joining flow — data integrity nit.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend test file /app/backend/tests/test_recruitment_prompts6to10.py loads REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL from frontend/.env as fallback (needed because pytest env doesn't inherit it). Tests are idempotent (each dispo test creates its own fresh lead), but they use pytest.<attr> to stash created ids between tests within TestCreateAndDuplicate/TestDetailNotesActivity — those two classes are dependent-in-order. The bulk_assign test grabs the first 2 leads by last_activity_at desc and reassigns to recruiter2; this will keep migrating the same 'top-of-list' pair unless caller re-seeds. If seed data is re-imported, all counts reset. Playwright quirk reminded: never put backslashes inside f-strings — use string concatenation.
